verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, specifically 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego'; R1: 'Splashing down in the Pacific Ocean on Friday near San Diego'; R3: 'off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm Pacific Ocean off San Diego; R2 directly states the exact distance range.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission splashed down on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: '8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'; R2: '8:07 p.m. ET' on 'April 10, 2026'; R1: '8:07 p.m. Eastern time' on 'April 10, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Exact date, time, and time zones match across sources, including PDT conversion.

verifications.claim: The crew of the Artemis II mission landed safely.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'textbook landing', 'happy and healthy'; R2: 'all four members of the crew were "feeling great, happy to be home"'; R5: 'safely splashed down'
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe successful splashdown and crew in good health post-landing.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission was a 10-day mission around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '10-day trip to the moon'; R1: 'NASA rounds up in calling it a 10-day mission'; R4: '10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly call it a 10-day mission around the moon, despite precise duration being ~9 days.

verifications.claim: The recovery team from the U.S. Navy was prepared to retrieve the capsule of the Artemis II mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Personnel from NASA and the U.S. Navy are already en route'; R3: 'combined NASA and U.S. military recovery team will be standing by'; R2: 'Navy divers practiced procedures'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm U.S. Navy recovery teams were prepared and en route pre-splashdown.

verifications.claim: The capsule and crew of the Artemis II mission were recovered by the Navy.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'hoisted them up... to the U.S.S. John P. Murtha'; R2: 'Navy divers... A Navy chopper will transport'; R3: 'teams from NASA and the U.S. military will extract the crew... to the USS John P. Murtha'
verifications.reasoning: Sources detail Navy divers, helicopters, and ship recovering both crew and capsule.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is the first crewed Artemis mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis I, an uncrewed flight to the moon in 2022'; R3: 'sending the first humans toward the Moon since 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Sources distinguish Artemis II as crewed after uncrewed Artemis I, confirming it as first crewed.
